newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BETIS HAVE LAST CHANCE TO CATCH REAL MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BETIS HAVE LAST CHANCE TO CATCH REAL MADRID.

text.p: Mathematicians will say that Real Madrid can still be caught at the top of the Spanish league but realists know that the interest is now the race for the runner-up spot and the second European Cup berth.

Real stretched their lead to eight points over second-placed Barcelona at the weekend and their match on Saturday against third-placed Betis, a further two points back, represents the last real chance for the chasing pack.
Betis have a game in hand, five consecutive wins and the league's best away record as they seek their first title since the 1930s.
Their major concern is whether striker Alfonso Perez who collected his fifth yellow card of the season in the 3-1 win over Extremadura, will miss the game through suspension.
Betis defensive giant Roberto Rios was lucky to escape a red card in the same match.
Barcelona's 2-0 defeat at Espanyol left manager Bobby Robson's future even more uncertain.
Four fans have even offered to pay Robson to leave immediately.
To add to Barcelon's woes, midfielder Luis Enrique Martinez was alleged to have hit a spectator after being insulted while leaving the Sarria stadium.
Deportivo Coruna accepted the resignation of coach John Toshack after the 2-2 draw in the Galician derby with Celta Vigo.
The Welshman was jostled by a supporter telling him to return home as he left the Riazor stadium.
Former Valencia coach Luis Aragones was expected to take over next season but second team coach Jose Manuel Corral has stood in as caretaker-manager.
Another coach with problems is Benito Floro whose Sporting Gijon broke league regulations by playing seven minutes of their 2-0 defeat by Racing Santander with five non-European Union foreigners.
